text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool g-pool-4 queue depth > 95% (queued=1850). Autoscaler attempted scale but reported scale_limit. Paging @sre_jake @oncall-sre.

sre_jake: paging in, reading alerts. grabbing logs now. rough ETA on impact?

mlops_lina: spike started ~11:00 UTC after rollout of model:v19.1 to canary. seeing avg_ctx_tokens jump ~2x which is causing prefills and kv-cache warmup amplification. dashboard: https://console.redwood/ops/dash/g-pool-4 

prod-eng-tyler: visible latency and errors on several customer routes, throughput per-GPU dropping ~2x. can we divert traffic back to v18.3 or kill the canary?

sre_jake: looking at autoscaler logs, looks like we hit a hard GPU quota in us-west-2 and k8s ramp limits. paste logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:07:02Z] autoscaler: desired=120 current=72 max=72 reason=scale_limit
[2026-03-15T11:07:02Z] pool_queue: queued=1850 inflight=230 avg_latency=1.8s
[2026-03-15T11:08:05Z] model:v19.1: avg_ctx_tokens=5200 baseline=2400
```

sre_jake: immediate plan (short):
1) reduce canary traffic -> rollback to v18.3 on canary routes
2) enable strict kv-cache eviction + PREFILL limits
3) temporarily clamp max_context for new requests to 4096 (reject oversize)
4) open emergency GPU quota request with cloud vendor

mlops_lina: patching rollout config now to move canary back to v18.3 for alpha routes (/model-route/alpha). Performing 20% -> 0% shift in 30s.

prod-eng-tyler: enabling prefill dedupe. runtime config change: 
```
curl -X POST "https://ops.redwood/api/pools/g-pool-4/config" -d '\{"PREFILL_LIMIT":1\}' 
```

infra_ellie: escalated to cloud support for additional GPU quota. cloud ticket opened (CT-987654). ETA ~120m. In the meantime we can spin extra nodes in eu-west as a stopgap but will increase latency for regional customers.

sre_jake: deploying nginx/runtime guard to reject huge contexts and cap concurrency. snippet:
```
# nginx inline check (placeholder)
if ($ctx_tokens > 4096) { return 413; }
```
Also flipping controller throttles to cap per-customer concurrent requests to 12 to limit single-tenant floods.

customer-success-maya: CS reports two enterprise customers seeing ~10% timeout/error rate. prepping customer comms.

prod-eng-tyler: FYI v19.1 changed tokenizer/chunking which increased kv-cache footprint per request. we should revert tokenizer change in the immediate next patch.

sre_jake: queue trending after mitigations: 
```
[11:10] queued=1850
[11:20] queued=820
[11:25] queued=360
[11:30] queued=120
```
Looks like rollback + PREFILL_LIMIT + concurrency caps dropping pressure. Autoscaler still at max due to cloud quota.

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-20260315-3120000123. severity=high. impacted pool=g-pool-4. impacted_customers=[enterprise-A, enterprise-B, 14 small apps]. https://incidents.redwood/INC-3120000123

oncall-bot: @pager_sre assigned: sre_jake

sre_jake: handing off to night oncall @sre_kim at 11:45 UTC. short summary for handoff: root cause likely model:v19.1 rollout increased avg_ctx_tokens and changed prefill behavior -> kv-cache warmup + larger per-request token counts. Autoscaler hit region GPU quota and ramp constraints (scale_deadzone). Mitigations applied: rollback canary -> v18.3, PREFILL_LIMIT=1, max_context clamp=4096 (reject large requests), per-customer concurrency cap=12, cloud quota ticket opened. Status: queues draining but degraded. Monitor until cloud quota or cross-region capacity is ready.

sre_kim: ack taking over. will monitor metrics and queue. escalate if queued > 500 for >10m.

mlops_lina: follow-ups created: 
- ACTION-1: postmortem and RCA for tokenizer change in v19.1
- ACTION-2: add pre-deploy load test that simulates context distribution and kv-warmup
- ACTION-3: expose autoscaler "scale_deadzone" metric + alert in console
- ACTION-4: rollout guardrail: fail canary if avg_ctx_tokens >1.5x baseline

customer-success-maya: draft to customers: "We experienced elevated errors and timeouts due to a new model rollout that increased request context sizes. We rolled back the canary and applied throttles; service has been restored for most customers. Engineering is investigating full root cause and will follow up with a postmortem." Will send after review.

sre_kim: incident downgraded to medium at 12:15 UTC. monitoring window 6h. leaving notes here for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

sre_jake: final note: please coordinate a staged re-introduction of tokenizer changes behind a synthetic load test and explicit autoscaler stress test. closing handoff.
